doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Playing without arrangements and the firehouse ending
summary: The band plays without arrangements under Marty's cues; Sherman explains the firehouse ending and Monk tells of Fiddler Williams calling 'Channel' for the bridge.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Wow. Well one thing you said about the band and this CD, our jazz does not rely on arrangements or even preparatory discussions before we swing into a tune.

Well that’s true. I can’t believe it but that’s what it is. We have a beautiful rapport in the band, we have fine leadership. Marty just says, “Okay we’re going to do this” and then one-two, off we go. And then for the endings, every once in a while he’ll throw a firehouse ending in on you and you just have a keep listening and you can watch him. Sometimes the bell of his horn will come up a little bit or his eyebrow will arch. You can tell.
Okay now you just used a term that I’m not familiar with. A firehouse ending?
Oh an extended, another four bars. Instead of just ending after four bars after the drum break, they’re going for eight bars.
That’s a firehouse ending. I taught you something. I can’t believe it.
Thank you. I will be prepared next time, in fact I’m going to use it, I’m going to use that firehouse. That’s cool. I wonder where that came from?
I don’t know. I don’t know. That’s interesting to find out, the origin of the phrase.
One time I had played with this veteran fiddler, Claude “Fiddler” Williams.
And he said, we were playing the song, we were playing like an Ellington song and we were almost done, and he said to the band, he goes, “Channel.” He said, “Channel.”
Uh oh is right, we didn’t know what he meant. And he meant the bridge. Channel, as in English Channel, or that was his term for the bridge and he wanted to go back to the bridge.
Wow. I never heard that, Monk.
